findings.title: `UsernameForm` calls a method overload that does not exist
findings.description: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only declaration in the repository is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160`; a grep over all `*.java` files finds no zero-argument overload. The `services` module will fail to compile. The call should pass the user, e.g. `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is inverted: passkeys are off for initial login and on for every re-authenticating user
findings.description:
The predicate returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. The code it replaces filled the WebAuthn form data when the user was **not** yet selected. The effects at the three call sites:

- **Initial login (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:115`)**: `context.getUser()` is null, so `fillContextForm` is never called and `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI` is never set. `passkeys.ftl:2` then renders no `webauth` form on `login.ftl` or `login-username.ftl`, so first-time passkey login disappears.
- **Error challenge (`UsernamePasswordForm.java:137`)**: after an unknown username the user is still null, so the re-rendered form also loses passkeys. `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:190` expects `username webauthn` at that point.
- **Re-authentication**: the passkey UI is shown to any user with a non-null context, whether or not they have a passkey credential. The new test comment at `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:304` says it should not be.

The tests in this same diff contradict the predicate: they assert the `webauth` form is present on the first `oauth.openLoginForm()` and expect automatic discoverable-key login.

The intended condition is most likely `user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`. With that, the `UsernameForm.java:47` guard also makes sense: skip the form on re-authentication only when the user has no passkey.

findings.title: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` does not test the scenario it names
findings.description:
The test sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` (line 282), so it only proves that nothing is rendered when passkeys are disabled for the realm. The case that matters for this change is untested: passkeys enabled for the realm, re-authenticating user has no passkey credential. That is exactly the branch the inverted predicate above gets wrong, so the suite would not catch it.

Smaller problems in the same test:
- Lines 291-296 and 312-317 use `try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {}`. This only works because `AssertionError` is not an `Exception`; the `nullValue()` assertion can never pass, and the blanket catch swallows any WebDriver failure. Use `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`, as `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:202` already does.
- The comment at line 280 ("set passwordless policy for discoverable keys") contradicts the code, which disables passkeys.
- `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey` and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` have identical first halves; the latter makes the former redundant.

findings.title: Re-authentication flag check is duplicated and adds a package cycle
findings.description:
`setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` re-implements the auth-note read and `Boolean.parseBoolean` that already exist in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257-260`). That method is still used at lines 129, 139 and 250, so there are now two sources of truth for the same flag.

To support this, `authenticators.util` statically imports `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `authenticators.browser` (line 35), while `browser` already imports `AuthenticatorUtils`. The constant was widened from `protected` to `public` (`AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:58`) solely for this.

Cleaner options: make the existing helper a public static method on `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` and have `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` (same package) call it, or move the constant and both helpers into one place.

findings.title: Missing `@Override` on `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators`
findings.description: The method overrides the new hook at `WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:128` but has no `@Override`, unlike the other overrides in this class (lines 41, 47). Without it, a later rename of the base hook would silently restore the default behaviour. The neighbouring `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` hook (`WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:147`) has a near-identical name and the same default, which is easy to confuse; a short Javadoc separating the two would help.

findings.title: `PasswordForm` now runs `fillContextForm` on bad-password challenges
findings.description: `PasswordForm` inherits `challenge(context, error, field)` and always has a user set. Previously the `context.getUser() == null` guard skipped WebAuthn setup there. Now each failed password on the password-only page generates a new challenge, overwrites `AUTH_CHALLENGE_NOTE` and sets passkey form attributes. `login-password.ftl` does not import `passkeys.ftl`, so nothing is rendered and the work is wasted. This persists for users with a passkey even after the predicate is corrected.

findings.title: Passkey re-authentication cannot switch to a different user
findings.description: With `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` returning false, `isUserIdentified` is `"false"` during re-authentication, so the browser may offer any discoverable credential. `WebAuthnAuthenticator.action` still compares the user handle against the user already in the context and rejects a mismatch with `WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER`, so the wider entry point does not allow swapping identity.

findings.title: Error paths keep the re-authentication form state
findings.description: `createErrorResponse` now applies `USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED` before re-rendering, matching `badPasswordHandler` at `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:222`. A failed passkey attempt during re-authentication therefore no longer falls back to the full username/registration form.

structured_findings.summary: `UsernameForm` calls a method overload that does not exist
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is inverted: passkeys are off for initial login and on for every re-authenticating user
`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` does not test the scenario it names
Re-authentication flag check is duplicated and adds a package cycle
Passkey re-authentication cannot switch to a different user
Error paths keep the re-authentication form state
